title: An Examination and Critique of Current Methods to Determine Exercise Intensity
authors: Jamnick NA, Pettitt RW, Granata C, Pyne DB, Bishop DJ
population: Review of methods to prescribe intensity relative to the moderate, heavy and severe domains (percent-of-max anchors, VT/GET/RCP, LT1/LT2, MLSS, CP/CS)
findings: Prescribing intensity as a fixed percentage of VO2max, VO2peak, HRmax or maximum work rate has little merit for eliciting distinct, domain-specific homeostatic perturbations.
There is some evidence supporting LT1, GET and VT as delineating the moderate and heavy domains.
There is little evidence supporting most commonly used methods to delineate the heavy and severe domains, with the exception of CP and CS.
Training studies are still required to verify whether different methods of prescribing intensity change training adaptations.
limitations: Evaluates construct validity through acute physiological responses, not training outcomes; narrative rather than systematic search.
implications: Define a three-domain zone model: LT1/VT1 as the moderate-heavy boundary and critical speed as the heavy-severe boundary; avoid fixed %HRmax cut-offs for those two boundaries.
Estimate CS from performance data and LT1/VT1 from HR/DFA-a1/RPE/talk-test proxies, and label which source defines each boundary.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (vol 50 pp 1729-1756, online 2020-07-30). Abstract confirms all findings.
